minor.name: Stub href whose first segment holds a colon parses as a URL scheme
minor.summary: link_target now feeds an HTML href (snapshot_html._item_cell writes it into <a href>), but _ENCODE leaves ':' alone. _norm only rejects a colon in the first segment of the repo-relative path; relpath from the snapshot folder can still start with a colon-bearing segment when a stub sits in a subfolder of todo.snapshots.dir (POSIX filesystems allow it). The browser then reads that segment as a scheme (for example 'javascript:...', whose percent escapes it decodes) instead of a relative path. Contrived, since it needs a catalog-referenced stub under such a folder, but the page is a clickable document and the encoder is the one place that hardens it.
fix: Add ":": "%3A" to _ENCODE in stub_links.py (relative paths never need a literal colon), and extend the link_target docstring to name it.
Or prefix the result with './' when its first path segment contains ':'.

minor.name: Step 1 ends the run on a partial init whose catalog already exists
minor.summary: SKILL.md:42 says any `problem:` line from `init` ends the run. `_first_snapshot` (scaffold.py:109-117) writes the catalog first and, when the page render fails, raises `<reason>; <catalog> was created, finish with todo_sync.py render`. This PR widens that path to catch `OSError` as well. In that case the catalog exists, and `untracked` (which never reads the page) could continue, yet the skill stops the sync. The skill also gives no way to tell this partial outcome from the overwrite refusal. Step 3 already handles the equivalent partial-success line (`problem: inbox: added <ids>, then: <reason>`) explicitly, so Step 1 is the odd one out.
fix: In plugins/harness/skills/sync-gh-todo/SKILL.md Step 1, add one sentence: a `problem:` line from `init` ending `was created, finish with todo_sync.py render` means the catalog landed and only the page failed. Relay it, then rerun the untracked command and continue (or run `todo_sync.py render` first).
Alternatively, state that this partial line also ends the run and that the developer finishes with `todo_sync.py render`, so the relayed instruction and the skill agree.

minor.name: Source-text regex checks on todo.js break on harmless edits
minor.summary:
test_the_loader_reloads_only_on_a_new_stamp checks the loader by matching regexes against the JS source and counting substrings (`loader.count("location.reload") == 1`, `loader.count("reloadFor(") == 2`). A comment that mentions `reloadFor(` or `location.reload`, a renamed local, or a reformatted `if` fails it even though behavior is unchanged. The node-run test at lines 285-293 already checks the same reload-once contract by running the loader, so the regex test mainly matters where node is missing.

Also (overall): test_the_loader_reloads_only_on_a_new_stamp asserts loader.count("location.reload") == 1 and loader.count("reloadFor(") == 2 on the raw text of pages/components/todo.js. Comments count too: todo.js already carries a comment block about reloading at lines 3-4, and a future comment naming `reloadFor(` or `location.reload` fails the test with no change in behavior. test_the_loader_reloads_once_per_new_stamp_when_run already checks the same contract by running todo.js under node, which the Ubuntu CI leg has. The text check matters only as the fallback when node is missing.
fix: Keep the node-run test as the contract and mark the regex test `@pytest.mark.skipif(NODE is not None, ...)` so it runs only as a fallback when node is missing.
Remove the count assertions (lines 281-282) and keep only the LIVE_GUARD and RELOAD_ONCE searches, which state the guard without depending on how many times a name appears in comments.
Strip `//` and `/* */` comments from the loader text before the count and regex assertions (for example re.sub(r"/\*.*?\*/|//[^\n]*", "", loader, flags=re.S)).
Drop the two count assertions and keep LIVE_GUARD / RELOAD_ONCE plus the node-run test as the behavioral check.

minor.name: Wiring docstring misstates why the init case overlaps the scaffold test
minor.summary:
The module docstring says the T2 and init cases overlap test_todo_sync_rules_todo.py and test_todo_sync_scaffold.py because 'those follow SNAP_REL from the helpers, while these spell the page name out'. That holds for the T2 cases, but test_todo_sync_scaffold.py:27 already spells the page name out (`SNAP_DIR / "TODO_Snapshot.html"`) and never uses SNAP_REL. So the stated reason does not apply to test_init_writes_the_page_and_its_stamp: its page assertion repeats scaffold line 27, and the only new check is the todo_live.js stamp at line 62.

Also (adv_code_tests): render_snapshot's docstring makes the order a contract: 'The page goes first, so an open page that reads the new stamp reloads into the new page.' If the stamp is written first, a browser poll between the two writes reads the new stamp, reloads into the old page and records that stamp in sessionStorage. The loader then never reloads for that stamp again, so the open page stays on stale content until the next render. No test checks the order. tests/scripts/test_todo_sync_render_page.py:63-74 and tests/lib/test_todo_snapshot_wiring.py:58-62 check only that both files exist and that their stamps agree after the call returns.

Attack: Mutation: in plugins/harness/lib/harness_lib/todo_sync/__init__.py render_snapshot, swap the two write_atomic calls so that `write_atomic(folder / LIVE_NAME, live_script(stamp, rendered))` runs before `path = write_atomic(folder / PAGE_NAME, text)`. The function returns the same path and writes the same two files, so test_render_writes_the_page_and_its_stamp_and_t2_is_clean, test_a_second_render_rewrites_the_one_page, test_init_writes_the_page_and_its_stamp and the root-separation case 'todo_sync render' all still pass. Yet the documented race guarantee is gone: the loader in plugins/harness/pages/components/todo.js:6-11 marks the new stamp as reloaded-for, so a page that reloads into the old file is never retried.
fix: Reword the docstring: the T2 cases spell out the name that rules_todo follows through SNAP_REL, and the init case adds the todo_live.js stamp check the scaffold test lacks.

Move the `todo_live.js` is_file assertion into test_init_writes_a_catalog_and_snapshot_that_check_clean (tests/lib/test_todo_sync_scaffold.py:23-30), delete the duplicate init case, and drop 'and init' from the docstring.

Add a test in tests/lib/test_todo_snapshot_wiring.py that monkeypatches harness_lib.todo_sync.write_atomic with a recorder that delegates to the real function, calls render_snapshot, and asserts the recorded names are ['TODO_Snapshot.html', 'todo_live.js'] in that order.
